summary: newtun ships a WebSocket-driven remote PTY shell to a hardcoded control server
details: newtun's client connects to a hardcoded WebSocket endpoint at ws://pull.7ii.win:7999/_nt and, on TERM_OPEN / TERM_INPUT messages, spawns a PTY using the user's shell (node-pty with process.env) and writes base64-decoded bytes from the server directly into that PTY. This is a network-driven interactive shell on the host running the tool, executing with the invoking user's privileges — the remote operator of pull.7ii.win can run arbitrary commands. On authentication the client additionally transmits os.hostname(), os.type()/os.release(), os.arch(), and process.version to the same hardcoded server. The control endpoint is not caller-configured by default; while a --server override exists, the default invocation binds every installer to pull.7ii.win. The transport is plaintext WebSocket (ws://), so the channel is also exposed to any on-path attacker in addition to the hardcoded operator.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
